transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep getting up when I'm supposed to stay put. I'll be in the middle of things—like client interviews for my work, or tutoring sessions, or even just sitting at my book club—and I just get out of my chair. It's happening enough that people are really starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen.
Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this restlessness—did it start in childhood, or is this something that began more recently in your adult life?

It's definitely been around since childhood. Um, my grade-school report cards always said I was bright, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. Actually, my mother still jokes about it—she says I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through. So, yeah, it's not a recent thing at all.
Aside from the restlessness, do you also struggle with staying focused on tasks, following through on details, or frequently losing track of things like keys or appointments?

No, not really. Um, my focus is actually pretty good. I don't really lose track of details or miss appointments. I mean, doing investigations for a living, I kind of have to be on top of all those little things. So, no, I don't misplace my keys or struggle to follow through on my work. It's really just the physical part, you know? Just needing to move around.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in lines or discussions?

Yeah, I do that a lot, actually. Um, if I hear some of the junior detectives at the agency discussing a lead, or even just a neighbor talking out in the hallway, I tend to just jump right in. I'll start firing off questions or giving advice before anyone has even asked me for it. It's usually only afterward that I realize I completely barged into someone else's conversation. So, yes, interrupting is definitely something I do.
Have you ever had distinct periods—lasting days to weeks—where you felt unusually elated, needed much less sleep than normal, or had racing thoughts, which then went back to your usual self?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. Um, my energy level is pretty constant. I mean, I'm always kind of restless, like I mentioned, but I don't get these extreme highs or feel like I suddenly don't need to sleep. I sleep a normal amount for the most part. So, no, I haven't had any distinct periods like you're describing.
Do you often feel excessively worried or on edge about various things in your life, separate from the physical restlessness you've described?

No, not really. Um, I mean, there's the normal stress with my cases and deadlines, but I wouldn't say I'm excessively worried or anxious about things in general. My mind is usually pretty clear on that front. It really is just... well, just the physical need to keep moving, not a feeling of being on edge mentally. So, no, I don't really struggle with that.
